name: Azarel
overview: Azarel was a male Levite, identified specifically as a Korahite, a subgroup descended from Korah. He is noted for being the eleventh chosen by lot among the singers, highlighting his role within the Levitical musical ministry. His designation as a Korahite places him within a significant priestly lineage responsible for temple worship.
namesAndTitles: The name Azarel means 'G-d [El] has helped,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning common in Hebrew names that emphasize divine assistance. This proper name, recorded in 1 Chronicles 12:6, reveals a recognition of God's help in his identity.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Azarel as a descendant of Korah, situating him within the Korahite family line. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are documented in the biblical record.
scriptureSignificance: Azarel's significance lies in his role as one of the Korahite singers chosen by lot, specifically as the eleventh among them, indicating his participation in the organized Levitical worship in Israel. His inclusion in the list of warriors and musicians in 1 Chronicles underscores the importance of the Korahites in both military and liturgical functions during the time of David. This highlights the divine order and structure God established for worship through the Levites.
